articles.title: Scientists Burned Their Own Scrolls to Solve a 2,000-Year-Old Mystery
articles.summary: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 C.E., it turned a library of scrolls into blackened lumps. Now scientists think they can read them without opening them — by looking for lead in the ink.

articles.title: That 'Clean' Smell Might Be Filling Your Home With Tiny Particles
articles.summary: Scented cleaners smell fresh, but they can react with air indoors and create billions of tiny particles — small enough to reach deep into your lungs. Unscented products and open windows can help.

articles.title: NASA's New Telescope Could See What Even James Webb Can't
articles.summary: NASA is designing a new space telescope called PRIMA that sees far-infrared light — wavelengths the James Webb telescope can't detect. If approved, it could launch in 2033 to study how planets and galaxies form.
